stem.en: A group of two or more similar things or people interconnected with each other is called a network. In a computer network, each connected device is called a:

explanation.en: Computers, printers, phones and other devices on a network are nodes (hosts).

stem.en: The first network, set up in 1969 by the US Department of Defense's research agency, which later grew into the Internet was:

explanation.en: ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network) connected a few university and research computers in 1969.

stem.en: The World Wide Web was invented by:

explanation.en: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN (1989–90) along with HTML, URLs and HTTP. Ray Tomlinson sent the first network e-mail; Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP.

stem.en: Which is NOT an advantage of a computer network?

options.en: Complete freedom from viruses and hacking
Sharing a printer among many computers

explanation.en: Networks enable resource sharing and communication, but they also expose computers to threats like malware and hacking.

solution.en: Networks enable resource sharing and communication, but they also expose computers to threats like malware and hacking.

stem.en: Data on a network is usually sent in small units, each carrying the address of the sender and receiver. These units are called:

explanation.en: Messages are broken into packets that travel independently and are reassembled at the destination.

stem.en: Connecting your smartphone to your laptop and wireless earbuds via Bluetooth forms a:

explanation.en: A Personal Area Network covers devices of one person within about 10 metres.

stem.en: Computers in a college computer lab connected through a switch form a:

explanation.en: A Local Area Network covers a room, building or campus, up to about 1 km.

stem.en: A cable TV network spread across a city is an example of a:

explanation.en: A Metropolitan Area Network covers a city, typically up to about 30–40 km.

stem.en: The largest WAN in the world is:

explanation.en: The Internet connects networks across countries and continents.

solution.en: The Internet connects networks across countries and continents.

stem.en: A bank connects its branches in Bengaluru, Delhi and Singapore so that any branch can access customer accounts. This network is a:

explanation.en: Networks spread across cities and countries are Wide Area Networks.

stem.en: Which device converts digital signals from a computer into analog signals for a telephone line and back?

explanation.en: MOdulator–DEModulator: it modulates digital data onto an analog carrier and demodulates it back.

stem.en: RJ45 is:

options.en: An eight-pin jack used with Ethernet cables

explanation.en: RJ45 (Registered Jack-45) is the 8-pin connector at the end of Ethernet (twisted pair) cables.

stem.en: Which device regenerates a weakened signal so that it can travel farther?

explanation.en: Signals weaken over distance (around 100 m for Ethernet cable); a repeater regenerates them.

stem.en: A hub sends incoming data to all its ports, while a switch:

options.en: Sends data only to the port of the intended destination
Also sends data to all ports

explanation.en: A switch learns the MAC addresses on its ports and forwards each frame only to its destination, reducing traffic.

solution.en: A switch learns the MAC addresses on its ports and forwards each frame only to its destination, reducing traffic.

stem.en: Which device connects two DIFFERENT networks and decides the best path for data using IP addresses?

explanation.en: A router forwards packets between networks based on IP addresses. A gateway is the entry/exit point to a network that may use different protocols.

stem.en: In which topology is every node directly connected to every other node?

explanation.en: In a fully connected mesh every pair of nodes has its own link.

stem.en: In a star topology, if the central switch fails:

options.en: Data travels around a ring instead

explanation.en: All communication passes through the central device, so it is a single point of failure.

stem.en: Which topology uses a single backbone cable to which all nodes are connected?

explanation.en: In a bus topology all nodes share one cable; a break in the backbone affects the whole network.

stem.en: A tree (hierarchical) topology is a combination of:

options.en: Star networks connected through a bus

explanation.en: A tree topology connects several star networks to a common backbone in a hierarchy.

solution.en: A tree topology connects several star networks to a common backbone in a hierarchy.

stem.en: How many links are needed to connect 6 computers in a fully connected mesh?
A MAC address is:

options.en: A 32-bit address assigned by the ISP
A 128-bit address used only on Bluetooth
A 48-bit physical address burnt into the network interface card

explanation.en: The MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique 48-bit (6-byte) hardware address of the NIC.

stem.en: Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?

explanation.en: IPv4 has four numbers, each 0–255, separated by dots. 300 is too large; the other two have the wrong number of parts.

stem.en: How many bits are there in an IPv6 address?

explanation.en: IPv4 uses 32 bits; IPv6 uses 128 bits to provide far more addresses.

stem.en: In the MAC address FC:F8:AE:CE:7B:16, the first three bytes FC:F8:AE identify:

explanation.en: The first 3 bytes are the Organisational Unique Identifier of the manufacturer; the last 3 bytes are the card's serial number given by that manufacturer.

solution.en: The first 3 bytes are the Organisational Unique Identifier of the manufacturer; the last 3 bytes are the card's serial number given by that manufacturer.

stem.en: Which statement is correct?

options.en: The IP address is fixed for life and the MAC address changes daily
Both MAC and IP addresses are always assigned by the ISP
MAC addresses are 32-bit and IP addresses are 48-bit
The MAC address of a laptop normally stays the same, but its IP address may change when it joins another network

explanation.en: MAC is a permanent physical address of the NIC; the IP is a logical address assigned by the network (e.g. by DHCP), so it can change.

stem.en: Which language is used to design web pages?

explanation.en: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) describes web pages; HTTP is the protocol to transfer them.

stem.en: The service that translates a domain name such as ncert.nic.in into an IP address is:

explanation.en: The Domain Name System maps human-friendly names to IP addresses; this is called name resolution.

stem.en: In the URL https://www.example.in/admission/form.html, the domain name is:

explanation.en: https is the protocol, www.example.in is the domain name, and /admission/form.html is the path to the resource.

stem.en: A smart electricity meter that sends readings to the electricity board over the Internet is an example of:

explanation.en: IoT is a network of everyday devices with sensors and software that exchange data over the Internet.

solution.en: IoT is a network of everyday devices with sensors and software that exchange data over the Internet.

stem.en: In the domain name ncert.nic.in, the top-level domain is:

explanation.en: Domain names are read right to left: .in is the top-level (country code) domain, nic is the second level, and ncert is a sub-domain.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): A switch reduces unnecessary traffic on a LAN compared with a hub.
Reason (R): A switch forwards data only to the intended destination port, whereas a hub broadcasts to all ports.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both true and R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): An IP address uniquely identifies a device across networks and never changes.
Reason (R): An IP address is a logical address assigned to a device when it joins a network.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: IP addresses can change (for example a new one is assigned on another network), so A is false; R is true.

stem.en: Which layout best suits the computers inside each building?

options.en: Bus topology with one long cable
Star topology with a switch in each building

explanation.en: A star with a switch isolates faults to single computers and is easy to manage; mesh is too costly and a bus or ring fails when the cable breaks.

passage.en: Sunrise College has three buildings on a 600 m campus: Admin, Science Block and Library. The Science Block has 50 computers, Admin has 20 and Library has 10. The college wants all computers to share one Internet connection and a common server, keep costs low, and make sure one faulty computer does not stop the rest. The longest cable run, between Admin and Library, is 250 m.

stem.en: Which device is needed on the 250 m cable run between Admin and Library?

explanation.en: An Ethernet signal weakens after about 100 m, so a repeater (or a switch that regenerates the signal) is needed on a 250 m run.

passage.en: Sunrise College has three buildings on a 600 m campus: Admin, Science Block and Library. The Science Block has 50 computers, Admin has 20 and Library has 10. The college wants all computers to share one Internet connection and a common server, keep costs low, and make sure one faulty computer does not stop the rest. The longest cable run, between Admin and Library, is 250 m.

stem.en: How many cables are needed to connect 6 computers in a full mesh topology?

explanation.en: In a mesh every node is linked to every other node: n(n − 1)/2 = 6 × 5 / 2 = 15 cables.

solution.en: In a mesh every node is linked to every other node: n(n − 1)/2 = 6 × 5 / 2 = 15 cables.

stem.en: A MAC address has ____ bits, and its first ____ bytes identify the manufacturer of the network card.

explanation.en: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes). The first 3 bytes are the Organisationally Unique Identifier of the manufacturer; the last 3 are specific to the card.

solution.en: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes).
The first 3 bytes are the Organisationally Unique Identifier of the manufacturer; the last 3 are specific to the card.

stem.en: Which device connects the computers of a LAN and forwards data only to the destination computer’s port, using MAC addresses?

explanation.en: A hub sends incoming data to all ports; a switch learns the MAC addresses on each port and forwards data only to the destination. A repeater regenerates signals and a modem converts digital data to signals for the line.

stem.en: Which medium carries data as pulses of light?

explanation.en: Fibre guides light by total internal reflection.

stem.en: Which wireless medium needs line of sight and is used for satellite links?

explanation.en: Microwaves travel in straight lines between dishes or towers.

stem.en: In packet switching, all packets of a message must follow the same path.

explanation.en: Each packet can take a different route; they are reordered at the destination.

stem.en: Twisted pair wires are twisted in order to…

explanation.en: Twisting cancels much of the noise picked up from nearby wires.

stem.en: Which address is fixed in the network card by the manufacturer?

explanation.en: The IP address is logical and can change; the MAC address is physical.

stem.en: Which network type connects a smartwatch to a phone?

explanation.en: A personal area network covers a few metres around a person.

stem.en: A switch sends every message to all connected computers.

explanation.en: That is a hub. A switch delivers only to the intended device.

stem.en: Which device holds the MAC address of a computer?

explanation.en: The MAC address is built into the network interface card.

stem.en: Which topology is a group of star networks joined by a backbone?

explanation.en: Tree (hierarchical) topology combines star and bus.

stem.en: Which protocol is used to download emails from a mail server to a device?

explanation.en: POP3 retrieves mail; SMTP sends it.

stem.en: Which markup language lets you create your own tags?

explanation.en: XML is extensible: tags are defined by the user.

stem.en: TELNET sends data, including passwords, without encryption.

explanation.en: That is why SSH has largely replaced TELNET.

stem.en: In the case study, why is Science chosen for the server?

explanation.en: Placing the server where most users are reduces traffic between blocks.

stem.en: Which protocol lets a WhatsApp voice call travel over the Internet?

explanation.en: Voice over Internet Protocol sends voice as packets.

stem.en: A service that stores a website's files on an always-online server is…

explanation.en: Hosting providers rent space on their web servers.
